text: According to indirect (representative) realism, the immediate objects of perception are:
choices: mind-independent physical objects, perceived without any mental intermediary
ways of being appeared to (e.g., sensing 'redly'), not objects of any kind
mental representations such as sense data, from which the external world is known only mediately
the physical object itself in veridical cases but a mental item in hallucination, with no element common to the two
explanation: Indirect realism posits a three-term structure (subject, mental representation, external object), so the immediate objects of awareness are always mental items like sense data, and the world is known only behind a 'veil of perception'. Option 0 is direct realism, which denies any such intermediary; option 1 is the adverbial theory, which reconstrues apparent objects as modes of sensing; option 3 is disjunctivism, which denies a common element across the good and bad cases. Only option 2 states the representationalist's immediate mental objects.
